findings.title: Desktop mixed results conceal continuation below an orphaned heading
findings.evidence: search-results--mixed__en-desktop-dark.png, bottom of results panel: “Tasks (2)” appears without either task, immediately above the keyboard footer. No visible scrollbar or continuation cue identifies the remaining tasks and AI row. The accessibility snapshot contains those options; src/components/shell/search/SearchDialog.tsx:606 caps the scroll area, while :652 renders group headings independently. The mobile mixed capture exposes its task and AI row clearly.
findings.fix: Keep the existing listbox and result order, but add an overflow-only continuation cue using border, surface, and muted-text tokens. Keep each group heading visible with its first option when sizing the viewport, and make the scroll affordance visible above the keyboard footer.

findings.title: Search interaction outcomes need runtime evidence
findings.evidence: The supplied screenshots and accessibility snapshots show selection and keyboard instructions, but do not demonstrate arrow navigation into offscreen tasks, Enter activation, Escape clearing then closing, focus return, or the mobile layout with the software keyboard open. Source handlers at src/components/shell/search/SearchDialog.tsx:373 and :433 establish implementation intent only.
findings.fix: Supply the relevant stage-gate runtime results for those interactions, including reaching the offscreen task and AI options and activating a mobile result with the software keyboard open.
findings.benchmark: Raycast: arrows and Enter; Escape clears then closes.

screens.reachesNineIf: Make continuation in desktop mixed results unmistakable and prevent a group heading from appearing without its first option.
The captured state already meets 9: it explains the miss, offers a query-preserving fallback, and keeps alternative destinations accessible.
The captured running state already meets 9, with the query retained, ordinary results distinguished, named progress, and a clearly labelled Cancel action.

findings.title: Repeated connection messages weaken the outage hierarchy
findings.evidence: shell-loading__th-mobile-light.png and shell-loading__en-mobile-dark.png: the header and content card repeat “Waiting for connection” around an already explanatory warning banner; the header copy is truncated. Desktop variants repeat it again under Current warehouse. src/components/shell/DesktopShell.tsx:195–213 confirms the header repetition.
findings.fix: Keep ConnectionNotice as the prominent outage explanation and recovery action. Shorten HeaderBrand's unresolved connection label and use a concise data-unavailable label in the existing LedgerPanelStatus, retaining the reserved content layout and existing tokens.

screens.reachesNineIf: Consolidate the repeated outage wording so the connection notice owns the explanation and the remaining placeholders identify only what is unavailable.
Already reaches 9 for the captured states: clear explanation, one recovery action, readable localisation and appropriate mobile targets.

findings.title: Retry feedback shifts the adjacent recovery action
findings.evidence: Comparing route-error__en-desktop-dark.png with route-error--retrying__en-desktop-dark.png, the retry button expands when its spinner appears, moving “Go to Finished goods” approximately 24px right. src/components/shell/PageFailure.tsx:79 conditionally inserts the spinner without reserving space.
findings.fix: Reserve a fixed spinner slot inside the existing Button, using the existing Spinner and spacing tokens, so both recovery controls retain their positions while retrying.

findings.title: Retry settlement is not demonstrated in this group
findings.evidence: route-error--retrying__en-desktop-dark.png captures the pending control; the supplied images do not show recovered product content or the settled result of another failed attempt.
findings.fix: Provide runtime evidence for retry after removing the simulated read failure and retry with the failure retained, checking restored content, repeat-attempt feedback and retained keyboard focus.

screens.reachesNineIf: Bring hierarchy to 9 by reserving spinner space so the recovery action remains stationary during retry.
